role.altitude: The athletic trainer keeps assessing injuries, agreeing rehab with physicians, running sessions and advising athletes face to face; rebuilding handouts and programs, and digging through injury notes for patterns, shrink.
skills_to_grow: Logging injuries consistently so patterns show
role.ambitious_version: A trainer who sees an injury trend in a team within weeks and changes the warm-up before more players get hurt.

tasks.short: Prepare instruction, instruct coaches, athletes, parents, medical personnel or community members in the care and prevention of athletic injuries, answer follow-up questions and record who was instructed.

steps.what: Athletic trainer prepares the instruction: topics, handouts and demonstrations
Athletic trainer instructs coaches, athletes and parents in the care and prevention of athletic injuries
Athletic trainer answers follow-up questions from athletes and parents
Athletic trainer records who was instructed

tasks.design: The trainer keeps a library of approved handouts and short videos per injury topic and age group, so instruction is assembled rather than rebuilt and attendees take the handout home, which cuts repeat questions. Attendance is ticked in the team app, which takes the same time as the spreadsheet. Instructing stays face to face.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handouts were rewritten for each group.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared handout libraries and team apps.
tasks.still_hard: Coaches who push athletes back too soon.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a coach to rest a key player.

reach.learn: Whether instructed coaches see fewer injuries.

evidence.claim: Patient information suits an answer desk quoting approved leaflets.

assumptions: Boundary: instructing others on care and prevention; treating injuries is outside.

Instruction and recording attendance keep their full time. s1 keeps 80 because handouts and videos are taken from the library and the trainer still fits them to the audience; s3 keeps 90 because the handout answers some repeat questions.

incremental.description: Athletic trainer keeps handouts current with guidelines.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly one-to-one instruction on varied topics, so the library helps little and s1 keeps 95, s3 keeps 100 (0.5); high: many group sessions on the same topics (5.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess the injury, collaborate with physicians to agree rehab goals, develop the rehabilitation program, implement it in supervised sessions and record progress for the physician.

steps.what: Athletic trainer assesses the injury with the physician's findings
Athletic trainer collaborates with the physician to agree rehabilitation goals and phases
Athletic trainer develops the rehabilitation program: exercises, loads and progression
Athletic trainer checks the final program: exercises, loads and phases against the goals agreed with the physician, and the athlete it is for
Athletic trainer releases the checked program to the athlete's app
Athletic trainer implements the program in supervised sessions
Athletic trainer records progress in the shared athlete record for the physician

tasks.design: Rehab programs are built from an exercise library with phase templates per common injury, which the trainer adapts to the athlete; the trainer checks the final program and releases it once to the athlete's app. Progress is recorded in the shared athlete record that the physician can read, which takes the same time as today. Assessment, agreeing goals and supervising sessions stay human.

approvals.approved_version: The rehabilitation program with exercises, loads and phases exactly as checked by the trainer in s3b, released once to this athlete's app; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Programs were written from scratch and progress reported by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Exercise libraries with templates and shared athlete records.
tasks.still_hard: Athletes who feel ready before the tissue is.
tasks.human_edge: Judging when an athlete can safely return.

evidence.claim: Health data are a special category under the GDPR.
Exercise libraries with templates speed up program writing.

assumptions: Boundary: from assessment to recorded progress; medical treatment is the physician's.
Athletes consent to sharing their record with the physician.
Assessment, goals, sessions, the program check and release, and recording progress keep their full time. s3 keeps 70 because phases and exercises come from the template and the trainer adapts them.
unknowns: Share of injuries with a standard template.
research_questions: Do athletes follow home programs better?

incremental.description: Athletic trainer keeps phase templates current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly rare injuries without templates, so s3 keeps 95 (0.4); high: common injuries in a large squad (4.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review injury records for patterns, judge the risks to address, plan comprehensive athletic injury or illness prevention programs, implement them in sessions and track participation.

steps.what: Athletic trainer reviews injury records to find patterns
Athletic trainer judges which risks to address and plans the prevention program
Athletic trainer writes the program and materials
Athletic trainer implements screening and prevention sessions
Athletic trainer tracks participation in the program

tasks.design: Injuries are logged in an injury register with fixed fields for body part, mechanism, activity and time lost, and a dashboard shows patterns per team and season instead of a spreadsheet the trainer sorts by hand. Judging the risks, designing and running the program stay with the trainer. Writing the program and ticking participation in the team app take the same time as today.
tasks.previous_blocker: Injury notes were free text and patterns had to be found by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Injury registers with dashboards and team apps.
tasks.still_hard: Getting athletes to keep doing prevention exercises.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a program athletes will actually do.

ambition.what: Review injury patterns monthly instead of once a season.

tasks.altitude: Less sorting notes; prevention work stays.

reach.learn: Whether injury dashboards change training plans.

evidence.claim: Registries can return figures to practitioners to compare with others.
Health data are a special category under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: planning and running prevention programs; treating injuries is outside.
Input contract for s1: injuries logged in the register by the trainers when they treat them, with fixed fields; older seasons stay in spreadsheets.
Judgement, writing the program, sessions and tracking participation keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because the dashboard groups injuries and the trainer still reads and interprets the patterns.
research_questions: Do injury rates fall after targeted programs?

incremental.description: Athletic trainer fills the fixed injury fields at each treatment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: much of the history stays in older spreadsheets, so s1 keeps 75 (4.0); high: injuries logged in the register for several seasons (9.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check fit and condition of equipment, advise athletes on the proper use of equipment, give written fitting guidance and note the advice.

steps.what: Athletic trainer checks the fit and condition of the athlete's equipment
Athletic trainer advises athletes on the proper use of equipment
Athletic trainer writes fitting guidance for the athlete
Athletic trainer notes the advice in the athlete record

tasks.design: Standard fitting sheets per equipment type, such as helmets, braces and shoes, are handed out instead of written each time, with the trainer adding what is particular to the athlete; advice is noted in the athlete record as today. Checking and advising stay hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance was written by hand for each athlete.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard fitting sheets and pick lists.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling that a brace sits wrong.

reach.learn: Whether fitting problems recur by model.

assumptions: Boundary: advice on equipment; buying equipment is outside.
Checking, advising and noting the advice keep their full time. s3 keeps 60 because the sheet gives the standard guidance and the trainer still writes the athlete's own fit notes.
unknowns: How often written guidance is given.

incremental.description: Athletic trainer updates fitting sheets for new equipment.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly custom fittings the sheets do not cover, so s3 keeps 85 (1.2); high: many athletes with standard equipment (3.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
